title: B=65 vs B=75 at the real production schedule
question: Does the sawtooth between two same-width batches survive production parameters?

schedule.note: first points ever measured at the full production schedule; wall clock only

why_this_pair: 65 and 75 are both vector width 1 (v2(B)+v2(L) = 0), so XLA treats them identically and what separates them is the unexplained sawtooth, not the width effect.

extrapolation_check.finding: The two errors point in OPPOSITE directions. Short cells are not a systematic upward bias as previously claimed; they are +/-2.5% noise in both directions.

gap_collapse.interpretation: The 5.7% that separated these two batches was a measurement artefact of the short schedule, not a property of the curve. At production they are indistinguishable.

per_kernel_us_per_sweep_replica.note: Measured on the SHORT schedule; tracing 4e6 sweeps would record ~56 million kernel launches and the profiler cannot sustain it.
per_kernel_us_per_sweep_replica.REFUTED_finding: XLA emits COMPLETELY DIFFERENT kernel sets for two batches of the same width, and the two programs cost essentially the same. This refutes the live hypothesis that the sawtooth comes from XLA picking better and worse programs by shape.
per_kernel_us_per_sweep_replica.correction_2026_10_18: REFUTED by the full PTX tracking in opstep_65_75.json. The kernel sets are NOT different: both batches compile to the same 43 kernels, and the three 'exclusive' kernels on each side are the SAME operations under different XLA-generated names, proven by identical PTX signatures (fusion_1458/fusion_1377 both ld_scalar=69, st=16; loop_log_plus_one_maximum_fusion_1/loop_maximum_negate_fusion_1 both ld_scalar=7, ld_nc=7, st=4). The conclusion that XLA program selection does not cause the sawtooth survives, but for the opposite reason: the program is identical, so selection was never in play.

scope_and_limits: One pair, two points, a single production run each with no repeats; 0.6% is within single-run resolution, so the correct statement is that the two are indistinguishable at production, not that B=75 is 0.6% better.

A +/-2.5% per-point noise can fabricate apparent gaps up to about 5%, which covers this pair. It does NOT cover the large sawtooth features: 18.5% between B=63 and B=65 on the T4, or the 20% dispersion across the 19 width-1 batches in [325, 525]. Those stand.
This does not touch the width effect at all: +29% to +118%, ten to forty times this noise, independently reproduced in raw CUDA and at the PTX instruction level.
supersedes_claim: My earlier prediction that short cells over-report by +2.6% to +12.9% systematically. Magnitude right (~2.5%), sign wrong.
